key_insight: Intrinsic electron trapping in amorphous silica depends on local strain and medium-range network flexibility, not a universal bond-length or bond-angle threshold.
engineering_relevance: Understanding these traps can inform efforts to reduce charge-induced degradation in silica-based logic devices or exploit charge localization in memory applications.
method: Generate 2,512 defect-free amorphous silica models using classical melt-quench molecular dynamics.
Statistically select a representative subset of 200 structures.
Use HSE06 density functional theory to characterize one- and two-electron traps and structural relaxation.
evidence_signal: Across the sampled structures, single-electron polarons have occupied states 3.1–4.3 eV below the conduction band minimum, while calculated bipolaron energy ranges are consistent with optical absorption features at 3.7, 4.7, and 6.4 eV.
watch_item: Results concern simulated defect-free bulk silica; interfaces, pre-existing defects, and device operating conditions may alter trapping behavior.
paper_title: Statistically Robust Characterization of Polaron and Bipolaron Intrinsic Traps in Amorphous Silica Reveals the Role of Network Flexibility in Electron Localisation
